title: Compass and Current
premise: Vesper Iversen, captain of the riverboat Kestrel, hauls contraband and cargo through a contested delta where three colonial concessions are about to expire and the maps are about to be redrawn. When a flood delivers a chest bearing the seal of a drowned republic, she finds inside the deeds that could return stolen land to the river communities—or make her rich enough to vanish forever. Hunted by a magistrate's enforcer, a concession magnate, and her own crew's doubts, Vesper chooses justice over invisibility, delivering the deeds to the villages before the permits lapse, at the cost of the Kestrel and nearly her life. The story ends with the river reclaiming the magnate's dredge, the concessions void, and Vesper rebuilding a smaller boat with the found family she never meant to gather.
about_author: Marguerite Nakamura is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six seasons charting monsoon rivers across three continents before turning to fiction. Her debut novel draws on her fascination with waterways as borders, witnesses, and accomplices.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Receipts
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A routine run up the delta introduces the Kestrel's ragged crew and the expiring concession permits looming over every transaction. Vesper refuses a lucrative job from magnate Corvin Ashe, valuing invisibility over coin. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, the quiet pride of a woman the river has never managed to drown.

chapters.title: What the Flood Surrendered
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. After a night storm, the Kestrel's snags a chest stamped with the seal of the Republic of Meridia, drowned forty years ago. Inside: land deeds and a ledger of Ashe's family's original fraud. Her deckhand Juno urges selling; engineer Bram warns of the enforcer Wray, already asking questions at the docks. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Rail
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Tobin Sela, a Meridian archivist's grandson, boards at a fueling post claiming to track the chest. Vesper doesn't trust him, but his knowledge of the deeds' legal weight—and of Wray's warrant—is undeniable. They strike a wary bargain. Emotional beat: suspicion slowly braided with recognition; two loners sizing up a shared enemy.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Hounds
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Wray boards the Kestrel under pretext of inspection; Vesper hides the chest in the bilge beneath a false floor while Bram fakes an engine failure. Wray leaves unconvinced, posting watchers at every lock. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension and the first crack in Vesper's invisibility—she has become a person of interest.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The monsoon arrives early, closing the high channels. The crew debates: run the dangerous interior route to reach the villages before the permits expire, or hole up and lose the window. Juno, an orphan of an evicted river town, casts the deciding vote for the interior. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing around shared grievance rather than shared profit.

chapters.title: Sandbar Justice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Grounded on a shifting bar, the crew must lighten ship; Tobin confesses he once sold information to Ashe's men and is seeking redemption, not just inheritance. Vesper must decide whether forgiveness is another kind of gamble. They winch the Kestrel free by moonlight, Wray's launch closing behind. Emotional beat: hard-won trust, the cost of honesty.

chapters.title: The Drowned Republic's Heirs
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. The Kestrel reaches the first Meridian-descended village, where elders remember the fraud in songs. Delivering the first deeds is triumphant—until word arrives that Ashe has bought the magistrate and moved the permit expiry up by two weeks. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into urgency; justice revealed as a race, not a gift.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Wray's launch rams the Kestrel at night; the chest is nearly lost overboard, Juno is wounded, and Vesper rams Ashe's dredge in retaliation, stranding his operation mid-river. She and Tobin are captured briefly and escape by diving the flooded rapids. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into purpose; Vesper stops running and starts fighting.

chapters.title: The Last Permit Day
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, climax. With the hull leaking and Wray blockading the final village's landing, Vesper runs the Kestrel through the flooded cut no captain has survived, delivering the last deeds as the permits lapse at dawn. Bram beaches the dying Kestrel deliberately to block Wray's launch; Ashe's claims void in front of assembled witnesses and a defected magistrate. Emotional beat: sacrifice crowned by vindication.

chapters.title: New Keel, Old River
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the crew salvages the Kestrel's bell and lays a keel for a smaller boat, the villages' first fair contracts already signed. Tobin stays; Wray, exposed, flees upriver; Ashe's dredge rusts where the river took it. Vesper, once invisible by choice, is now known by choice. Emotional beat: quiet belonging—the river forgives nothing, but it keeps its own kind.
